build: tape version 1, cracked to disk by Oneway (R-TYPE++), level-skip key added

exclude: zero page: pointers and the sprite multiplexer's tables, written at run time before they are read
variables: the stage number, the enemy slots' program state, bullets, explosions and the boss's rows, each written before it is read
the stage's map, built at run time by build_map ($162F) from the stage's block lists, or copied there for the battleship
the play area's characters $00-$BF, copied at each stage's start from the stage's own file ($86AC) by copy_stage_chars ($11FA); described with the stages
screen memory and sprite pointers; the crackers' loader also puts its depacker here ($CD00) while the screen is off
work space: stage1_setup ($1224) clears $FD40-$FF3F, and what it holds in play is written at run time
9 parts: Level 3, Level 6, Level 5 and others
8 parts: Level 6, Level 5, Level 3 and others
elsewhere: 9 parts: Level 3, Level 6, Level 5 and others
8 parts: Level 6, Level 5, Level 3 and others

comments.text: The processor port's data direction register; scroll_side writes $2F to it each time it shifts the screen.
The processor port: $35 in play (RAM at $A000 and $E000, I/O in), $34 while the code writes under the I/O, $36 with the KERNAL in for loading.
The tape loader's leftover entry: JMP $8000 then JSR $1794, three bytes each, never run in this crack (nothing jumps to $0812 or $0815).

Cold start of the game, entered from $5F0A once the program is unpacked. Clears $3384-$3396 and the stack, clears $0334-$07FF, saves the zero page from $02 into $0677-$0776 (so the KERNAL's own values can be swapped back for loading, see swap_zero_page), zeroes the stage number $0200 and the next-stage flag $0310, masks every interrupt, points the IRQ vector at the KERNAL's $EA31 and calls the crackers' loader at $6200 to load stage 1. The NOPs at $086A-$087F fill the space where the tape loader's call sat.
Sets up a new game: initialises the variables (init_players), the screen and colours (clear_screen, init_video), then falls into new_life.

Starts a life or a stage: builds the stage's map pointers (reset_stage), clears the sprite tables (stage_pointers, stage_setup, build_map), asks the stage code for its colour set ($637C with X/Y = $6D40), sets $0B5E to 3, starts the stage's music ($6379 with X = 0), turns the screen on and shows READY or the player number (show_message), then runs the play loop from $08C1.

The top of play: shows the lives icons for the player whose turn it is (show_lives with the count from $281D or $281E), then waits on the state in $0B5D. State 2 is a life lost: it shows message 1 and goes back to $08F5 to restart the stage from the last restart point; state 1 shows message 0 (READY). A stage won ($0232 or $0310 set) leaves through $0978. Otherwise it rebuilds the scroll position from the restart table restart_columns indexed by the stage.

Restarts the stage at the right point: $0202 = $9A marks the scroll as not yet started; while the scroll position $0201 is past the restart column in restart_columns for this stage, it steps the map back (reset_stage) until it is not. Then it reloads the map pointer $7A/$7B from $7AD4/$7AD5 (the stage's map start) and joins new_life's tail.

After a stage is won: waits twenty frames (counting $0977, which the raster interrupt sets every frame), and if $0233 says so takes the stage's own background colours from stage_colour1/stage_colour2 into $021E/$021F. Then clears $0232 and, with $0310 set, goes on to load the next stage at $0978.
Operand of the LDY at $0949, the stage-end wait's count: the crackers' loader writes 0 there and their skip key $13.
Set non-zero by the raster interrupt at $0D1C every frame (the value it wrote to $D018); cleared by whoever waits for the next frame ($096B, $1504).

Entered when a stage ends, won or lost. Counts the turn ($281F), and in a two-player game ($2819 says whose turn) switches players when the other one still has ships. A switch shows message 2 and restarts the other player's stage one back ($0200 is decremented, then reloaded). Otherwise it fades to the end-of-stage sequence at $09C5.

Waits for raster line $C4, resets the stack, blanks every interrupt and turns on only sprites 0-2. With no player left ($2820 two-player flag and both players' lives at $281D/$281E spent) it shows GAME OVER (message $80) and goes to $0A4E. Otherwise it plays the stage's end tune ($6379 with A = 2) and runs the screen for $0290 frames (counter $0B60/$0B61), moving the ship sprites to their resting place (park_ship) and running the stage, explosion and sound updates ($6370, draw_bits, animate_force) each frame.

Stops the stage (stage code $6373), resets the scroll counters $280D-$2810, turns off sprites and raster interrupts and points the IRQ vector back at the KERNAL ($EA31), swaps the KERNAL's zero page back in (swap_zero_page) and, unless the stage number is $D3 (the ending: then it jumps to $5FB1 with $C3/$C4 = $6800), banks the KERNAL in ($01 = $36) and calls the loader at $6200 for the next stage's three files. The NOPs fill the tape loader's old call. Back from the load it swaps the zero page again and starts the stage at new_life.
Swaps the 256 bytes from zero page $02 onwards with the copy at $0677: the game's own zero page goes out and the KERNAL's comes in, or back, either side of a load.

One frame of the ship coming to rest after a stage: sets the sprite pointers of sprites 1 and 2 to $44 and $45 and moves sprites 1 and 2 (and sprite 0 too when $32 = 1, the Force docked) one pixel at a time towards Y = $64 and X = $A0, handling the X high bit in $D010.
What the play loop waits for: 0 in play, 1 waiting for fire at READY, 2 a life lost. Written by show_message and the stage-end code; read by the play loop and the raster interrupts.
Set to 3 by new_life and by the player switch at $09B4; also used at $32B6, $32C0 and $57A9. Its meaning is open.
Non-zero once the first frame of the stage has been drawn; the raster interrupt at $0E49 sets it.
Frame counter, low and high bytes ($0B60, $0B61), for the end-of-stage sequence at $09C5 ($0290 frames).
Fade_count: the frame counter's high byte.
The byte after fade_count, read with it.
Frames show_message waits before it starts reading the fire button ($32 = 50).
Per stage (0 to 7), the scroll position a life restarts from: the map is stepped back to the first restart point before this column.

Shows one of the screen messages and waits for fire. A = 0: READY; A = 1: the per-player message (PLAYER ONE or TWO, from $2819); A = $80: GAME OVER. It copies the message's characters into two rows of screen memory at $CD1F-$CD5D from the tables at $0C5B-$0CD4, colours those rows white ($D918, $D940), then, each frame, swaps the multicolours either side of raster lines $42 and $82 and runs the stage code ($6370), until $32 frames have passed and fire is pressed. It then clears the sprites and the message, puts the raster interrupt on line $CA with the handler at $0DE6, and steps the state $0B5D down.
The characters of READY in the game's own font, top row ($0C5B) and bottom row ($0C69): letters two characters wide and two high, with $00 as a space.
READY's bottom row of characters.
The characters of GAME OVER, top row ($0C77) and bottom row ($0C91).
GAME OVER's bottom row of characters.
The characters of PLAYER, top row ($0CAB) and bottom row ($0CBC), followed by the digit ONE ($0CCD, $0CCF) or TWO ($0CD1, $0CD3).
PLAYER's bottom row of characters, then the digits.
Msg_player_low: the digit ONE, top row (at $0CCD, byte 17 on).
Msg_player_low: the digit ONE, bottom row (at $0CCF, byte 19 on).
Msg_player_low: the digit TWO, top row (at $0CD1, byte 21 on).
Msg_player_low: the digit TWO, bottom row (at $0CD3, byte 23 on).
Draws the lives at the bottom left of the status panel: clears the eight cells at $CF49-$CF50, then puts the ship character $1F, in colour 9, in as many of them as A says (bits 0-2).

The interrupt entry the vector at $FFFE names while the KERNAL is banked out: saves A, X and Y on the stack as the KERNAL's own entry does, reads the break flag (and ignores it, the BEQ the KERNAL has here is a NOP) and jumps through $0314, which the game sets to each raster handler in turn.
The NMI vector at $FFFA points here: an RTI, so RESTORE does nothing.

The raster interrupt at the top of the play area. Sets the fine scroll ($020C into $D016), the character set ($30; on stage 2 the value in $64 instead, when it is not zero), sets $0977 for the main loop, the background colours ($021E, $021F), and the sprites' X positions and high bits for the five sprites the multiplexer uses ($82-$86, $91-$95). Then picks the next raster handler: $585D on line $0398 when $024C is set (the boss), $114C on line $023E when $0235 is set, or $0F6C on line $023A. With $0221 set and $024E clear it also runs flash_ship and $34FB. Last, unless a message is up ($0225) or the stage has not started ($0B5F), it runs the sprite logic at $17FB, or $5902 during the boss.
Operand of the JMP at $0DC7 in irq_top, a byte other code writes or reads by its address.
High byte of the JMP at $0DC7: the scroll routine for the stage, written by its set-up ($34FB side-scrolling, $3702 battleship).

The raster interrupt at line $CA, above the status panel: moves the five multiplexed sprites off to X = 0, on stage 3 writes $4F to $D011 (extended colour mode on), sets the panel's colours, character set ($32) and scroll ($18), and chains to $0EC5 on line $D6. Then, with interrupts on again, it runs the stage code once ($6370) and, on the first frame of a stage, sets $0B5F.

In play (not paused, $024E clear): moves the player and the Force ($3D74, skipped once the stage is won), runs the stage's end check (ship_explodes); when the stage has just been won ($0232 set, $0233 clear) sets the state $0B5D to 1, or 2 in a two-player game. Then calls the stage's own per-frame routine at $940A.
Operand of the JSR at $0E68 in b_0E5B, a byte other code writes or reads by its address.
High byte of the JSR at $0E68: the frame hook (player_frame in play, ship_explodes while dying).
Operand of the JSR at $0E82: the low byte of the stage's frame hook, written by stage_pointers.
Operand of the JSR at $0E82: the high byte of the stage's frame hook.

The pause: while paused ($024E set) fire unpauses. Then it reads the keyboard: row 0 ($DC00 = $FE) column 3 ($DC01 = $F7) is F7, which pauses unless the stage is won. Puts the keyboard lines back, clears $0B5F and returns from the interrupt.
The common end of the raster handlers: interrupts on, Y, X and A pulled from the stack, RTI.

The raster interrupt at line $D6: turns extended colour back off ($D011 bits 5-7 cleared), then positions the first band of multiplexed sprites (sprites 3 to 7, each where its flag at $044C-$0450 is set): Y from $A0-$A4, the sprite pointer at $CFFB-$CFFF from $AF-$B3, colour from $BE-$C2. Their X positions go in at the top of the screen ($0D04), so the band is ready before the top line. Chains to $0F4D on line $FF.

The raster interrupt at line $FF: sets the vertical scroll and screen-on bits ($020B or $10 into $D011), and chains to irq_top ($0D04) on line $30. It ends through the crackers' level-skip check at $6290, which the original ended with a plain return.

The raster interrupt on the line in $023A: writes the Y positions of the second band of multiplexed sprites (from $A5-$A9, each where its flag at $0451-$0455 is set) while the first band is still being drawn, then chains to $0FB7 on the line in $023B.

The raster interrupt on the line in $023B: gives the second band's sprites (3 to 7, flags $0451-$0455) their X positions ($87-$8B), X high bits ($96-$9A, merged into $D010), pointers ($B4-$B8) and colours ($C3-$C7). Chains to $1066 on the line in $023D.

The raster interrupt on the line in $023D: sets the character set from $64, then writes the Y positions of the third band of multiplexed sprites ($AA-$AE, flags $0456-$045A), and chains to $10B6 on the line in $023E.

The raster interrupt on the line in $023E (also reached from irq_top when $0235 is set): gives the third band's sprites their X positions ($8C-$90), X high bits ($9B-$9F), pointers ($B9-$BD) and colours ($C8-$CC), then chains to irq_panel ($0DE6) on line $CA. Unless paused, it runs the sound and effects routine at attack_script.
Operand of the LDA at $1151: the raster line of a band split, written by the stage set-ups.

While the ship is invulnerable after starting a life ($1190 positive), flashes sprites 1 and 2 (the ship) on and off every frame for $78 frames (counter $1191), then makes it vulnerable again ($1190 = $80) and turns every sprite on.
Bit 7 set: the ship can be hit; the collision check at $319C returns at once while bit 7 is clear. Cleared at the start of a life, set again by flash_ship.
Frames of flashing left before the ship becomes vulnerable ($78 at the start).
Clears screen memory from $CC00 to $CEF7 to character 0, in three passes of 256 bytes from $CC00, $CD00 and $CDF8: the play area and the status rows.

Draws the whole play area from the map at the current scroll position: twenty rows ($13 down to 0) of forty characters, from the map at $0201/$0202 minus $27 (map rows are $200 bytes apart), into the screen at $CC00, and each character's colour from the stage's colour table at $8CAC into colour RAM at $D800. The column index is kept in the operand at $11DB. Stage 3 ($0200 = 2) clears the screen instead.
Operand of the LDY at $11DA: the column draw_screen is on.

Copies the stage's characters $00-$BF, six pages from $86AC-$8CAB (the start of the stage's second file), to $C000-$C5FF, the lower three quarters of the play area's character set (the top quarter, $C600-$C7FF, holds the resident shots and explosions).

The stage set-up for stage 1 (the first entry of the table at $139A). Points the interrupt's per-frame jump at $0DC7 to scroll_side and the band line operand at $1152 to $CA, sets the lower band's character set ($64) to $38, the copy at $E000, turns every sprite to multicolour and none to double width, and clears the 512 bytes at $FD40-$FF3F. Then the star field: the 17 star characters $AF-$BF are cleared in the stage file's character source ($8C24) and in the copy at $E578, and, unless the scroll is already at the end ($0202 = $9B or $0201 at least $D3), the twinkle timers are reset ($94C4 to $94CA, $94B8 to $94BE) and six stars are set as single pixels ($80) in the source ($8C3C-$8C77) and three in the copy ($E590-$E5CB). Then it jumps to the stage's own set-up at $9531, which places the boss's tail.
The stage set-up for stage 2: character set $30, points the operand at $3685 at the colour table $8CAC, and clears the battleship flag $134C.

The stage set-up for stage 3, the battleship. Points the interrupt's per-frame jump at $0DC7 to $3702 and the band line operand at $1152 to $C6. The first time (while $134C is clear) it clears the map at $9A00-$B3FF and draws the ship into it: 23 rows of $4F bytes from $8E6C, laid $82 bytes apart from $9EBA. Then resets nine bytes of the ship's state at $3AD7-$3AE2, points $3ADA/$3ADB at $9E3B, and jumps to $394A.
Non-zero once stage3_setup has drawn the battleship into the map, so a restart does not draw it again.

The stage set-up for stage 4: the per-frame jump at $0DC7 back to $34FB, the operand at $3685 to $8CAC, the band line at $1152 to $CA, character set $30; clears $8C44-$8CAB, copies six bytes each from $91E1 to $91E7 and $91D5 to $91DB, and puts $80 in six object slots at $8C5C-$8C97.
The set-up routine for each stage, a word each, low byte first: $1224, $12A7, $12BB, $134D, then $17FA (an RTS) for stages 5 to 8. stage_setup ($161B) writes the chosen one into the JMP at $162C.
The high bytes of the set-up words, read at $1626 with the low bytes at $139A.
For each stage, a word: the address of the list of blocks the map is built from (read by build_map, $162F).
The high bytes of the block-list words, read at $1641.
For each stage, a word: the stage's own routine that the interrupt calls once a frame through the JSR at $0E82 (written by stage_pointers, $15F0); $17FA, an RTS, for stages that need none.
The high bytes of the frame-hook words, read at $1608.
For each stage, the background colour 1 ($D022) used after the stage is won ($0949).
For each stage, the background colour 2 ($D023) used after the stage is won.
For each stage, the low byte of the scroll position where the stage's end is reached; copied into $36A9 by stage_pointers.
For each stage, the high byte of the same position, into $36AA ($00 for stage 3, whose end is the battleship).

Sets up the video chip for the game: screen off, black border and background, video bank 3 ($C000-$FFFF, $DD00 bits 0-1 cleared), screen at $CC00 and characters at $C000 ($D018 = $30), multicolour text in 40 columns ($D016 = $18), the background multicolours, all sprites on and multicoloured, and every sprite register from $D000 to $D010 set to zero.

Puts the ship back at the start of a life: makes it invulnerable ($1190 = 0), clears $D010 and $0236, clears the first 30 bytes of the even and second half of the odd sprite shapes $40-$49 in the RAM under the I/O chips ($D000-$D27E, ten stretches, with $01 = $34 while it does; the video chip reads its sprites there, so these are shapes the game draws itself), turns every sprite on in multicolour with the ship's colours and pointers ($44, $45), and sets the ship's starting position ($25 = $3F, $2B = $72) and speed ($021D = 4). If the Force is in play ($32 non-zero) and a stage has just been won ($281C or $0310 set), it keeps the Force, one level down if it was at 3 ($33), placed beside the ship; otherwise it clears the Force ($31-$34) and parks its sprite. Clears $0310 and $281C and jumps to $2E9C.

Resets the stage to its start: clears the state $0B5D, the frame flag, the sprite slots of every object table ($242F, $3ED5, $40AA, $4791, $4C4F, $4EAC, $3385) and the multiplexer flags $044C-$045A, and the variables $020C-$0263, $02A8-$02FF and $7A-$D1. Unless a stage was just won, $1FF0 = $D3. Puts the scroll at its start ($0201/$0202 = $9A27), points the NMI vector at $0D03 and the IRQ vector at $0CF4, banks the ROMs out ($00 = $2F, $01 = $35), sets the default raster lines of the multiplexer ($023A-$023F = $4F, $64, $67, $77, $8C, $8F), character set $30, the scroll registers, points the stage-end check at $0E68 at $2821, the map's first pointer from $7AD2/$7AD3, and fills the status row at $CF58-$CF6D with character $1A.
Turns off both CIAs' interrupts (and acknowledges them) and turns on the video chip's raster interrupt alone.

Copies this stage's values from the tables into the code that uses them: the end column (stage_end_column_lo, stage_end_column_hi) into $36A9/$36AA, the frame hook (stage_frame_hooks) into the JSR at $0E82, and a pointer from $207C into $2068/$2069.
Calls this stage's set-up routine: writes the stage's entry from stage_setups into the JMP at $162C and jumps through it.
Operand of the JMP at $162C in stage_setup, a byte other code writes or reads by its address.
High byte of the stage set-up's address in the JMP at $162C, written by stage_setup.

Builds the stage's map at $9A00 from its list of blocks (stage_block_lists). Each entry is three bytes, or five when bit 7 of the first is set; $FF ends the list. The first byte picks a block (bits 0-6) whose address comes from the tables at $8E6C/$8ECF; the block starts with its width and height. The second byte is the column and the third the row (with bit 7 adding $100 to the column); a five-byte entry also gives how many times the block repeats across and down. Each block is copied into the map row by row (map rows are $200 bytes apart), skipping zero bytes so blocks can overlap, and stops at the bottom of the map ($C000).
Operand of the ADC at $1789: the size of the block-list entry just read, 3 or 5, written by build_map at $1668 and $1677.

Code the crack never runs (only the dead JSR at $0815 names it): copies $1000 bytes from $8E53 to the RAM under the I/O chips at $D000, the status panel's characters from $8B63 to $CEF8 with colours looked up in $5F61, and six pages from $8C53 onwards to $C600-$CBFF. It reads like the tape version's set-up after its load.
An RTS: the set-up routine for stages 5 to 8 and the frame hook of stages that have none.

Run from the interrupt once a frame in play: for each of the fifteen multiplexed sprite slots whose flag at $044C,x is 1 (an object alive), tests what touches it. Pickups (pointer $4A, $5B, $5C or $5D) and objects coloured $81 skip the Force and bit tests. The Force (X $27/$28, Y $2C), and the top and bottom bits when present ($3079, $307A, at the ship's Y $2B less $13 or plus $0D), destroy what they touch through $1A30. Then the ship itself (X $25/$26, Y $2B): a pickup is collected (collect), anything else kills the ship through $319C. Then shots: the object's position is turned into a screen cell ($02C6 column, $02D5 row, $02A8/$02B7 the row's address from $2F72/$2F8B) and the two-by-three cells under it are read; the player's shots are characters $CC and up. A plain shot ($CC-$D3 or $DA-$E4) costs the object one hit point (it is removed and spawns an explosion from the six slots at $242F); the beam ($D4-$D9) costs $428C times 4 plus 2; $E5-$EC cost 5. Hit points are kept at $045B,x (from $1A30): an object with points left flashes (colour $81) with a hit sound ($11, or $13 for one whose colour has bit 7 set); one with none left is destroyed (kill_object). Objects coloured $12 also leave a mark in the map (character $B2).
Operand of the SBC at $1A66: the damage a beam does to an enemy's hit points ($045B), its width times four plus two, written at $1A5F.

An object's hit points are gone: plays an explosion sound (play_sound with $0E for a big object, $0C or $09 by colour), and either destroys every object in the same band as a big one (Y within $20, setting each to the explosion shape $61 colour 7), or turns this one into an explosion (pointer $61, or $65 for objects of type 2 at $0587,x), and sets the score to add in $3388. Objects with pointers $78 and $79 instead drop a pickup (drop_pickup).

Turns a destroyed carrier (pointers $78, $79) into the pickup it holds: colour and pointer from pickup_colours/pickup_pointers by the object's kind at $046A,x, then gives it a slow drifting path ($0479-$04F1 and $7C-$7F) and starts it moving (load_x_program, load_y_program).
The colour of each pickup a carrier can hold, by kind 0 to 5: $06, $07, $02, $08, $08, $0E.

The sprite pointer of each pickup, by kind: $5B three times (laser crystals of three colours), $5C (speed), $5D (missiles), $4A (a bit). The six bytes after it ($1B55-$1B60) are not read by this code.

The ship has touched something. A bit ($4A) gives the top bit, or the bottom one if the top is already there ($3079, $307A). A laser crystal ($5B) brings the Force: the first one ($33 = 0) creates it ($32 = $80, $33 = 1); later ones raise its level ($33, up to 4; at level 1 a second step is added when the Force is docked, $022A), and while it is docked its position is set beside the ship. The crystal's colour picks the weapon (the pointer from weapon_lo/weapon_hi into $3B99/$3B9A, place_force). Speed ($5C) raises $24 to at most 5. Missiles ($5D) set $1FF0 = 1. Anything else is an enemy: the ship dies ($319C). The pickup is removed from its slot, a sound is played (play_sound with $16) and the frame goes on.
By the crystal's colour (0 to 7), the low byte of the weapon routine the Force fires with.
By the crystal's colour, the high byte of the same routine.
Weapon_hi: the high byte of the red crystal's routine ($4CB3), which fire compares with the current weapon at $3B9E.
Collecting a pickup that is not a crystal: $5C raises the ship's speed ($24) up to 5, $5D gives the homing missiles; any other sprite touched kills the ship.
Operand of the LDX at $1C42 in j_1C0C, a byte other code writes or reads by its address.

Finds the object a homing missile should aim at: for each live slot whose pointer is $8A or more (an enemy that can be targeted), the distance in rows ($02D5 against $02E4) and columns ($02C6 against $3EED); keeps the slot in $1FEC and copies that object's screen address and column into $1FED-$1FEF. The comparison at $1CAB-$1CAF uses operands written into the code ($1CAC, $1CAE, $1CB0).
nearest_target: The comparison at $1CAB-$1CAF uses operands written into the code (the byte at $1CAC).
Operand of the ADC at $1CAD in nearest_target, a byte other code writes or reads by its address.
Operand of the CMP at $1CAF: the nearest target's distance so far, cleared at $1C4F and updated at $1CB3.

Launches a pair of homing missiles when the ship has them ($1FF0 positive), no message is up ($0777), the ship is low enough ($2B at least $3A) and neither missile is in flight ($1FD8, $1FD9). Finds a target (nearest_target), then starts both from the ship's screen cell ($3EED-$3EEF): one a row above and one a row below, with the direction and character set to their defaults (character $DE, a five-frame delay in $1FEA/$1FEB) and both marked in flight.

Turns missile X towards its target once its delay ($1FEA,x) has run out: compares the target's screen address and column ($1FED-$1FEF) with the missile's ($1FDA/$1FDC, $1FDE) and sets its horizontal step ($1FE4: 1 left, 0 none, $80 right), vertical step ($1FE6: 1 up, 0 none, $80 down) and the character that shows its heading ($1FE8, one of $DE-$E5, eight directions). Level with its target it looks for a new one.
Operand of the LDX at $1DB5: the missile slot, saved at $1DAF across the call to nearest_target.

Moves both homing missiles one cell a frame, if the ship has missiles ($1FF0 not negative). A missile in flight puts back the character it covered ($1FE0, colour $1FE2), steers, steps across and up or down (stopping at the edges of the play area, $CC00 and $CED0, and at column $26), and draws itself again in its heading's character, colour 15. Where it lands on solid background (the stage's character flags at $8D6C) or on another object's character it ends, and an object it hits starts an explosion (start_explosion). A missile launching first draws a trail character $F2 that counts up to $F3.
Operand of the LDY at $1EC6: the missile's column, saved at $1EC0 across the call to steer_missile.
Moves the screen pointer $DA/$DB (and its colour RAM twin $DC/$DD) down one row, 40 bytes.
Moves the screen pointer $DA/$DB and $DC/$DD up one row.
Two bytes, one per missile: 0 not flying, $80 flying, 1 launching.
Missile_state: the second missile's state.
The two missiles' screen addresses: low bytes at $1FDA/$1FDB, high bytes at $1FDC/$1FDD; column $1FDE/$1FDF.
missile_screen: low bytes at $1FDA/ (the byte at $1FDB).

The stage-end check hook at $0E68 points here in play (reset_stage writes it): the ship's whole frame. Runs the Force's launch and recall (force_control), reads the joystick in port 2 ($DC00 into $23) and dispatches on the eight directions (diagonals first, from $2CF7) to move the ship and tilt its sprite; with the stick centred it eases the tilt back (shape_step_down or shape_step_up by the tilt in $31). Then the Force: a free Force ($32 negative) wanders (force_wander) unless it is being recalled, and if it comes close it docks (from $2953); a docked one ($32 positive) is moved with the ship and checked against the background (force_background) and the explosions (animate_force). Then the two bits, each tested against the background a row above or below the ship (destroying what they touch, bit_hits_wall), and last the ship's own two cells against the background: any solid character (stage flags at $8D6C) kills the ship ($319C).

A bit has touched breakable background at ($29),y: starts an explosion over it in a free slot (start_explosion), or, for characters from $C0 up, draws the debris character $C1 and a one-cell explosion.

A free Force that comes within reach of the ship (vertically within $1A, horizontally within $18 in front or $14 behind) docks: in front ($022A = 1, the Force's level dropping from 3 to 2) or behind ($022A = 0, rising from 2 to 3), placed by the offsets at $2FC5-$2FC7, with $32 = 1, its weapon set (place_force), the recall cleared and sound 5 played.

Space (bit 4 of $DC01) launches or recalls the Force. A docked Force ($32 positive) is thrown forwards or backwards (by which side it is on, $34 = 1 or $80, sound 3) and flies eight pixels a frame until it hits something ($59) or reaches the edge of its range, then becomes free ($32 = $80). A free Force is called back: it moves three pixels a frame towards the ship across ($2FD2) and up or down ($2FD3) until it is level with it.

A free Force drifts on its own: every few frames (random from the CIA timer, up to seven) it picks a new random speed and direction across ($2FD9) and down ($2FDA), bounces back at the edges of the play area (X $17-$128, Y $38-$AE), and its weapon is updated (place_force).

Tests the cells the Force covers against the background (its size by level: force_width wide, force_height high): a solid cell makes a free Force bounce (flipping its directions in $2FD9/$2FDA, $59 set); a breakable one is destroyed by an explosion (start_explosion), or with the debris character $C1 for characters from $C8 up. The cell under the Force's top left is kept in $40CE-$40D0.

The ship has hit something. Unless it is flashing after a new life ($1190 positive), it dies: the frame hook at $0E69 becomes the explosion ($31FC), the bits and the Force are lost, the joystick is ignored ($23 = $FF), the ship's sprites become the explosion's (hires, white) and sound 4 plays. The C64-Wiki's tape-v1 poke for infinite lives writes RTS here.

The frame hook while the ship dies: every four frames ($32C9) it steps the explosion sprite on a shape and colour (blue, light blue, white from $32CA, two steps by $32C8). Then the sprites are cleared and the life is taken: in a one-player game a life goes from $281D and the lives are redrawn (show_lives), or at none left the game is over (to $5E47, $281F set to $D3). The unused two-player branch swaps players instead (switch_players), and when one of them is out it can move the stage on ($0200, $0310). Last, the stage code's entry 1 ($6379) is told the ship has died, once ($0B5E = 3).

Game over: the screen is cleared, the stage code silenced ($6379, A = 1), GAME OVER shown (show_message $80), the stack reset and the interrupts set back to the KERNAL's ($EA31). Then the tape prompt: "PLEASE REWIND TAPE", "THEN PRESS", "F1 TO START", waiting for F1 (key code 4 in $CB). Two more lines, an "OR" and a two-player choice, are in the table but the loop at $5EAA loads them (LDA) where it should store them, so they never appear, and only F1 is accepted: two_players is set to the key code less 4, always 0.
